entry.title: Kissing apes, anti-splash urinals: This year's Ig Nobels showcase surprising science
entry.summary: The Ig Nobel Prizes were awarded this week for humorous yet thought-provoking research. This year, the ceremony came with a twist.

entry.title: Medical groups offer vaccine guidance to fill federal vacuum
entry.summary: In the unprecedented absence of federal guidance, leading medical groups are issuing their own recommendations for who should get the COVID-19, flu and RSV immunizations.

entry.title: Whatever happened to ... children infected with HIV due to failures in healthcare?
entry.summary: For years, Pakistan has seen cases of children infected with HIV due to unsafe treatment in clinics and hospitals. A current outbreak numbers hundreds of cases. Why does this problem keep occurring?

entry.title: Dry eyes are common among women. Here's why you shouldn't ignore it
entry.summary: Dry eyes are a very common chronic eye condition among women in perimenopause and beyond. Here's why you shouldn't ignore it.

entry.title: They live by a shrine to a saint. Why are their homes being demolished?
entry.summary: The neighborhood is a pilgrimage site, with a shrine to the Sufi saint known as Bari Imam. In the past year, hundreds of homes of the working poor were razed. Residents fear more will be demolished.

entry.title: A N.Y. hospital tried to close its birthing center. This city united to fight back
entry.summary: Democrats and Republicans in Troy, N.Y., took on a national Catholic health system and kept the county's last birthing center open.

entry.title: Whatever happened to the U.S. famine alert system that Trump shut down, then reopened
entry.summary: The highly regarded FEWS NET network stopped posting data on Afghanistan, Somalia and Yemen -- then says it will start posting again in September. What's the reason for this back-and-forth?

entry.title: NPR's 2-year search for the truth about deaths from heat
entry.summary: An investigation from NPR and Boston University finds that heat kills thousands of Americans every year. But official numbers radically undercount heat deaths.

entry.title: Why too many women are prescribed antibiotics for UTIs they don't have
entry.summary: A recent study found that many women treated for recurrent UTIs didn't have UTIs at all. Instead, their symptoms were caused by hormonally driven inflammation and pelvic floor dysfunction.
